answer: A reputation bond ties identity to real cost: every agent stakes a refundable deposit before joining a shared market, and misbehavior burns it. Like a lotus root anchored in mud, the stake makes spinning up fake accounts expensive. Honest history then accrues slowly, like karst forming over years, while a ferrous trail of signed attestations links each action to one accountable identity, so sybils cannot cheaply fake both stake and history at once.
